QuestionStmt.S: Which from following cations will form most stable complex with same ligand?

Solution.S:
The stability of complexes formed by divalent metal ions with the same ligand follows the Irving-Williams series. According to this order, the stability increases from Mn²⁺ to Cu²⁺, with Cu²⁺ forming the most stable complexes among the first-row transition metals. The general trend is:

Cu²⁺ > Ni²⁺ > Co²⁺ > Fe²⁺ > Mn²⁺ > Cd²⁺

This order arises due to a combination of factors including ionic size, crystal field stabilization energy (CFSE), and the Jahn-Teller effect, which contributes extra stabilization for Cu²⁺ complexes. Among the given options, Cu²⁺ is placed at the highest position in this stability series, so it forms the most stable complex with a given ligand.

Thus, the correct option is Cu²⁺.
